title: Registry entry
description: Contract for edges E2 (author -> N2, registry entry shape written by a publish PR, ADR-0058 Section 2), E8 (N5 -> N4 -- write-back: build-pipeline N5 writes source_archive, source_sha256, signature, key_id, published_at, status into a `pending` version object (transition T1, ADR-0121)) and E10 (N2 -> N7, the site build's read side) in docs/architecture/depgraph.md. One instance of this schema is the full registry entry for one mod namespace:name, stored at mods/<namespace>.<name>/entry.json in this repository (see README.md). Ownership and version-object shape follow ADR-0058 Section 2 exactly; reserved namespaces (mc, test) use the identical owner shape bound to the organisation's numeric id instead of an individual's (ADR-0119 Section 2) -- this schema does not distinguish the two cases, by design. Mutability rules for this document are NOT expressed here (JSON Schema validates one snapshot, not a diff between two): see contracts/append-only.rules.md, edge E4, for what a PR may change.

id.description: namespace:name, the mod's registry identifier (ADR-0013: namespaced ids; ADR-0030: "id (namespace:name)"). Frozen forever once the entry is created -- contracts/append-only.rules.md.

owner.description: ADR-0058 Section 2, verbatim: "owner = { provider, id, name_at_registration }". Binds the namespace to a numeric account id, never to a username string, so that recycling a username can never capture a namespace (the attack this ADR exists to prevent). For a reserved namespace (ADR-0119) this is the organisation's numeric id -- the binding mechanism is identical, only the derivation of who owns it differs (ADR-0119 Section 2).

provider.description: The git-hosting provider the account id is scoped to, e.g. "github", "gitlab", "sourcehut" -- a free-form identifier, not an enum of known providers, because the registry format itself must not be provider-specific (ADR-0058 Section 4: "the registry format is provider-agnostic"). Nothing in this schema requires this value to be "github".

id.description: The NUMERIC account id on that provider -- never a username string (ADR-0058 Section 2). This is the field the registry CI compares to authorise a PR; accepting a string here (a username) is exactly the namespace-capture vulnerability ADR-0058 Section 2 exists to prevent, so the JSON type is deliberately "integer", not "string".

name_at_registration.description: The provider username/display name at the moment the namespace was created, kept for humans reading history (ADR-0058 Section 3's confirmation text names the account by this). It is NOT used for the ownership comparison -- only owner.id is (ADR-0058 Section 2), because usernames can be renamed or recycled and owner.id cannot.

versions.description: Append-only (ADR-0041: "Versions are immutable; existing hashes can never be updated, only new versions added", as amended by ADR-0121: a version is born `pending` and changes in place only by the transitions T1 `pending -> published`, T2 `published -> removed` and T3 `pending -> rejected`). Every element is one version in one of four states (`pending`, `published`, `removed`, `rejected`), each with an exact key set: see the `oneOf` below. At least one element exists once the entry is created, because the first publish PR (ADR-0058 Section 1) carries id, version, commit hash and source URL together -- an entry with zero versions is not a state this schema admits. Ordering and what a later PR may change to this array: contracts/append-only.rules.md.

items.description: ADR-0121's version object. The four states and their exact key sets (enforced by `oneOf`, one branch per `status`): `pending` = version, commit, source_url, status (what the author's PR can know, edge E2); `published` = those four plus source_archive, source_sha256, signature, key_id, published_at (written back once by the pipeline, edge E8, transition T1); `removed` = the nine published keys plus `reason` (takedown, transition T2); `rejected` = the four pending keys plus `reason` and `build_log_url` and none of the five pipeline-written fields (transition T3). Item-level `properties` below state every pattern once; each branch picks its keys. A schema validates one snapshot, not a transition: which state may follow which is contracts/append-only.rules.md.

version.description: Semantic version (semver.org 2.0.0 grammar). ADR-0030: "version (semver)"; ADR-0042 depends on strict semver semantics (patch/minor/major) for update policy.

commit.description: Full 40-hex-character git commit SHA-1 the pipeline fetched and built (ADR-0058 Section 1: "the pipeline fetches that exact commit"). Lowercase hex, matching git's own canonical rendering.

source_url.description: The author's public git repository URL, any host (ADR-0058 Section 4: "the source requirement is 'a public git repo', not 'GitHub'"). Accepts a normal scheme:// URL on any scheme/host, or the scp-like SSH shorthand (user@host:path) -- never restricted to a github.com hostname.

source_archive.description: URL of the pipeline's own archived copy of the exact built commit -- platform storage, not the author's repo (ADR-0041: "the registry points at our copy"; depgraph N6 artifact-store). Written back by the pipeline (edge E8, transition T1); present only in `published` and `removed` versions.

source_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the archived source tarball, lowercase hex, 64 characters (ADR-0041: "SHA-256 of every artefact is written into the registry entry by the pipeline; the launcher verifies after download").

signature.description: Platform signature over the archived artefact (ADR-0041: "every artefact is signed with the platform key"). Only presence/non-emptiness is enforced by this schema -- the exact encoding (depgraph edge E9: minisign/Ed25519 detached signature) is owned by contracts/signature-format.md, outside this task's declared scope.

key_id.description: Identifies which signing key produced `signature`, for rotation (ADR-0041: "the format carries key_id for rotation"). Exactly 16 uppercase hexadecimal characters: the 8 key-id bytes embedded in the minisign public key, reversed and hex-encoded, copied from the public key file's own comment line. Defined by contracts/signature-format.md (depgraph edge E9), section "Deriving `key_id`"; task 065 enforces it here.

published_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when the pipeline wrote this version back into the registry (transition T1).

status.description: Closed enum of four states (ADR-0041 as amended by ADR-0121): a version is born "pending" (not installable, no artefacts); the pipeline's write-back makes it "published" (T1) or, if its build is rejected, "rejected" (T3, terminal, never installable); a takedown makes a published version "removed" (T2, terminal) ("Only legal grounds ... lead to removed: artefacts pulled, registry entry kept with status and reason"). Whole-mod "deprecated" is a separate, page-level flag (ADR-0059 Section 2, see page.schema.json) -- not a value of this field, because deprecation marks the mod, not one version, and remains editable without touching immutable version objects.

reason.description: Required exactly when status is "removed" (ADR-0041: a removed version's "registry entry [is] kept with status and reason") or "rejected" (ADR-0121 Q-J: why the build failed); forbidden at "pending" and "published". The `oneOf` below enforces that presence and absence by status. That the text is non-empty after trimming whitespace is not expressible here (`"   "` satisfies minLength 1) and is checked by the transition rules in contracts/append-only.rules.md.

build_log_url.description: ADR-0121 Q-J: a link to the full build log of the rejected build. Present only when status is "rejected"; an https URL.

oneOf.description: pending: exactly version, commit, source_url, status.
published: the pending keys plus the five pipeline-written fields; no reason.
removed: the nine published keys plus reason.
rejected: the pending keys plus reason and build_log_url; none of the five pipeline-written fields.
